title: SharePoint admin center: item-level report on Everyone and Everyone except external users permissions
notes: claim 46: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the unqualified low-cost rating means indirect costs only, but the documented licensing routes can require a paid licence or add-on. The navigation, PowerShell commands, role requirements and report limits are supported; assurances about permission changes and end-user notifications need narrower wording.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-09-01T23:00:02.
The report provides item-level permission details where Everyone or Everyone except external users are recipients.
claims.quote: This report provides exact item-level permission details for every item where the special SharePoint groups Everyone except external users (EEEU) or Everyone are the recipients.

claims.claim: Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups is a SharePoint Advanced Management snapshot report.
claims.quote: The Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups report is one of the Data access governance snapshot reports available with SharePoint Advanced Management.

claims.claim: An administrator generates the report on demand.
claims.quote: Select Run report under either Content shared with 'Everyone' group or Content shared with 'Everyone except external users' group.

claims.claim: The download is a ZIP containing a CSV of items with direct or indirect group access.
claims.quote: The download is a ZIP file that contains a CSV file listing all items where that group has direct or indirect access.

claims.claim: Each report row identifies one item and its hierarchy of identifiers.
claims.quote: Each row identifies a single item that either group can access, along with the full hierarchy of identifiers from your organization down to that item

claims.claim: The CSV identifies the permission level granted.
claims.quote: Role definition | Permission level on the item. Has values such as Full control, Read, Edit, Contributor, Creator, or Viewer.

claims.claim: The CSV identifies a sharing link where applicable.
claims.quote: LinkId | ID of the sharing link, if applicable

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: ParentGroupName identifies the parent group when access is indirect.
claims.quote: ParentGroupName | Name of the parent group, when access is indirect

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: TotalUserCount is the number of users who accessed the item at least once.
claims.quote: Number of users who accessed the item at least once. The item is already shared with all internal users or with everyone, so this number tells you the actual exposure.

claims.claim: Everyone and Everyone except external users each have a separate report.
claims.quote: The report is available for two special SharePoint groups, and each group has its own report.

claims.claim: The report covers SharePoint and OneDrive across the tenant.
claims.quote: The above cmdlet generates a detailed report for all content shared with 'Everyone except external users' (Sites, groups and files) across both SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts, as of report generation time.

claims.claim: The report cannot be scoped to a single workload.
claims.quote: The report covers both SharePoint and OneDrive. You can't scope the report to a single workload.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Permissions for system files and system groups are excluded.
claims.quote: The report doesn't include permissions granted to EEEU or Everyone for system files and system groups.

claims.claim: An exclusion is Everyone inside Style Resource Readers on classic publishing sites.
claims.quote: For example, the report doesn't include the Everyone group inside the Style Resource Readers group. In classic publishing site templates, the Style Resource Readers group controls read permissions for the Master Page Gallery

claims.claim: The existing site permissions report identifies overshared sites rather than the individual items this report identifies.
claims.quote: While the site permissions for your organization report tells you which sites are overshared, this report tells you exactly which items are overshared and how access was granted

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Microsoft positions the report for scripted cleanup rather than relying on individual site owners.
claims.quote: Use this report when you want to find exactly where oversharing happens in your organization and fix it through scripting, rather than depending on individual site owners to review and modify permissions.

claims.claim: Content shared with these groups is visible to every internal user.
claims.quote: Content shared with these groups is visible to every internal user

claims.claim: Content shared with these groups surfaces directly in Microsoft Copilot search results.
claims.quote: it surfaces directly in Microsoft Copilot search results, which makes cleanup critical for Copilot adoption.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report is admin-opt-in: an administrator must assign its required role and initiate generation.
claims.quote: A Global administrator must assign the SharePoint Advanced Admin role before you can run this report. Select Run report under either Content shared with 'Everyone' group or Content shared with 'Everyone except external users' group.

claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint sites files special groups Everyone detailed permissions report automatic scheduled run enable disable notifications. Read the report page, DAG overview and PowerShell guidance/reference; no separate on/off switch or automatic execution was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: The advanced role permits viewing file names, paths and URLs across SharePoint content.
claims.quote: Standard SharePoint administrators and Global administrators can't view file properties across sites they don't own. The SharePoint Advanced Management Administrator role lets you view file names, paths, and URLs, and modify permissions as appropriate.

claims.claim: The report can reflect data from up to 48 hours before generation.
claims.quote: Reports capture data from up to 48 hours before generation.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Running the report is read-only, changes no permissions and starts no automated cleanup.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint detailed EEEU Everyone snapshot report read only permission changes automatic remediation notifications. Read the report page, DAG overview and PowerShell guidance/reference; none explicitly guarantees no permission writes or automated cleanup.
claims.fix: Replace the read-only/no-permission-change/no-automated-cleanup assurances in Risk assessment, Governance controls and the rationales with: 'The report captures the permission state of these groups at a specific point in time; Microsoft describes remediation as a subsequent action.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-detailed-eeeu-everyone-permissions-report.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft lists restricted access control, Change history and Site access review as remediation options for DAG findings.
claims.quote: Use Restricted access control (RAC) to limit access to a specific group. Review the 'Change history' report to identify recent permission changes that might have led to oversharing. Use the Site access review feature to request that site owners review and update permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions

claims.quote: You can run reports again every 30 days.

claims.quote: Make sure that the site permissions for your organization report is generated at least once.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is mixed: the listed base subscriptions plus a Copilot licence assigned to at least one user, SharePoint K/P1/P2 with the Plan 1 add-on, or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: At least one user in your organization is assigned a Microsoft Copilot license. Your subscription includes SharePoint K, P1, or P2, and your organization purchases the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on. Your organization has Microsoft 365 E7

claims.claim: The listed base subscriptions are Office 365 E3/E5/A5, Microsoft 365 E1/E3/E5/A5, or Microsoft 365 GCC/GCC-High/DoD.
claims.quote: Your organization must have one of the following base licenses: Office 365 E3, E5, or A5; Microsoft 365 E1, E3, E5, or A5; Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC-High, or DoD

claims.claim: E5-only DAG access excludes snapshot reports and remedial actions.
claims.quote: IT administrators with Microsoft 365 E5 licensing can access Data access governance reporting, but can't view or use the other SharePoint Advanced Management features. The reports don't provide snapshot reports or remedial actions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The pages read publish no separate price or meter for this particular report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Advanced Management detailed EEEU Everyone permissions report billing pricing charge meter. Read the report page, SAM prerequisites, DAG reports, PowerShell guidance/reference and SAM overview; no report-specific price or meter was stated.

claims.claim: DAG reports are unavailable for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet even with the required licences.
claims.quote: The reports are currently unavailable for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet, even if you have the required licenses.

claims.claim: The report requires Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell 16.0.27215.12000 or later.
claims.quote: This report requires module Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell version 16.0.27215.12000 or later, published April 30, 2026.

claims.claim: An unqualified low-cost rating, meaning indirect costs only, fits all the documented licensing routes.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; licensing.model: "mixed"; 'a subscription that includes SharePoint K, P1 or P2 plus the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on'. The standard defines low as 'indirect cost only: admin time, communications, training'.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'medium'. Replace the cost rationale with: 'Medium. Tenants without an existing qualifying entitlement may need a Microsoft Copilot licence or the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on. For tenants already entitled, the work is admin time to run the report and act on findings.' Keep the published licensing conditions unchanged.

claims.claim: End users are not notified when the report runs.
claims.quote: Searched: "sites and files" "report" "notifications"; SharePoint detailed EEEU Everyone snapshot report read only permission changes automatic remediation notifications. Read the report page, DAG overview and PowerShell guidance; no end-user notification guarantee was stated.
claims.fix: Remove 'end users are not notified or changed by it' from the impact rationale. Retain 'Low. Only administrators who hold the SharePoint Advanced Management Administrator role see the report.'

claims.claim: The published SharePoint admin center path reaches Run report for Content shared with 'Everyone except external users' group.
claims.quote: expand Reports, and then select Data access governance. Under Snapshot reports, in the Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups section, select View reports. Select Run report under either Content shared with 'Everyone' group or Content shared with 'Everyone except external users' group.

claims.claim: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsers -ReportType Snapshot generates the detailed EEEU report.
claims.quote:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsers -ReportType Snapshot
The above cmdlet generates a detailed report for all content shared with 'Everyone except external users' (Sites, groups and files) across both SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts

claims.claim: Using -ReportEntity Everyone instead generates the Everyone report.
claims.quote: To generate the report for Everyone, change the ReportEntity parameter value: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity Everyone -ReportType Snapshot

claims.claim: DetailedEEEUParameterSet takes ReportEntity and ReportType, with no Workload parameter.
claims.quote:
DetailedEEEUParameterSet
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>
    -ReportType <ReportTypeEnum>
    [<CommonParameters>]

claims.claim: Availability of this specific detailed special-groups report in GCC, GCC High and DoD remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint detailed Everyone special groups report GCC High DoD availability. Read the report and DAG pages plus service-description and Copilot-licensing table excerpts; government support is listed for other linked reports, not this specific detailed report.

claims.claim: SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance is the starting route for running these reports.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, in the navigation pane, expand Reports, and then select Data access governance. Under Snapshot reports, in the Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups section, select View reports.
claims.fix: Expand the abbreviated route to: 'SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance > Snapshot reports > Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups > View reports > Content shared with the selected group > Run report'. The full route in controls[0].ui is already correct.

claims.claim: The controls table covers all the controls the governance checklist asks administrators to set or check.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Ask a Global administrator to assign ... the role'; 'Generate the site permissions ... report once'; 'using the remedial options'. Table: only 'Running the item-level report for Everyone except external users or Everyone'.
claims.fix: The role assignment, prerequisite site-permissions report generation and referenced remedial options have no table rows. Do not add rows in this correction; label these checklist steps as prerequisites or follow-up actions documented in the cited Learn pages, rather than controls located by this table.

claims.quote: Standard SharePoint administrators and Global administrators can't view file properties across sites they don't own.
